title: S&P 500 earnings calls citing 'AI'
description: Share of S&P 500 earnings calls on which the term 'AI' was cited, per FactSet's full-season transcript search. Counts any mention of the term, not workforce-specific discussion. Before Q4 2025 FactSet reported only the count, so the share is count ÷ 500.

sources.title: Highest Number of S&P 500 Companies Citing “AI” on Q1 Earnings Calls in Over 10 Years

sources.title: Earnings calls citing 'AI' surge in 2025 as 'uncertainty' mentions fade

sources.title: The "AI Job Apocalypse" Is a Complete Fantasy
sources.excerpt: AI-as-augmentation out-mentions AI-as-substitution on earnings calls by ~8:1. Software Development jobs (both by count, and a percent of the overall job market) have been increasing since the beginning of 2025. The aggregate effects of AI on employment are "basically null" per recent academic research, with some evidence of reallocation between jobs and tasks.

sources.title: S&P 500 Earnings Season Update — Q1 2026 (AI mentions)
sources.excerpt: FactSet S&P 500 Q1 2026 earnings-season update (published May 8, 2026 with 89% of S&P 500 having reported actual Q1 results). AI citations: 'about 65% of S&P 500 earnings calls have cited the term AI so far,' slightly below the prior quarter's 68% (which was the highest percentage going back at least five years). AI remains substantially elevated vs historical levels. Overall Q1 2026 earnings performance: 84% of reporting companies beat EPS estimates; aggregate earnings 18.2% above estimates. Co-trending terms: 'Middle East' and 'oil' both at 5-year highs alongside AI.

sources.title: Highest Number of S&P 500 Earnings Calls Citing “AI” Over the Past 10 Years
sources.excerpt: Final full-season count for the Q1 2026 reporting period (calls conducted March 15 through June 11, 2026), by John Butters. "Overall, the term 'AI' was cited on 337 earnings calls conducted by S&P 500 companies during this period." "This number also reflects 68% (337 out of 498) of the earnings calls conducted by S&P 500 companies during this period." "This number is well above the 5-year average of 164 and the 10-year average of 103." Supersedes the May 8 in-season update (65%, taken at 89% reported), which was an interim rather than a final.

sources.title: More Than 65% of S&P 500 Earnings Calls for Q2 Cited “AI”
sources.excerpt: Final full-season count for the Q2 2026 reporting period (calls conducted June 15 through September 14, 2026), by John Butters. "FactSet searched for the term 'AI' in the conference call transcripts of all the S&P 500 companies that conducted earnings conference calls from June 15 through September 14." "Overall, the term 'AI' was cited on 331 earnings calls conducted by S&P 500 companies during this period." "This number reflects 67% (331 out of 493) of the earnings calls conducted by S&P 500 companies during this period." "This number is well above the 5-year average of 178 and the 10-year average of 114." "This marks the 3rd consecutive quarter that the term 'AI' was cited on more than 65% of the earnings calls conducted by S&P 500 companies." Sector leaders by count: Information Technology (72) and Financials (67); by share: Information Technology (97%), Financials (91%), Communication Services (90%).
